messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — did a quick portability probe: FlashFusion on SM89 vs SM92 across CUDA12.3 and CUDA13.1. seeing weird KV-cache thrash on SM92 with triton kernels :thinking:
Kevin: can you paste the exact bench command you ran?
Maya: sure
Maya: `./bench/run_attn_bench --model llama-7b --seq 2048 --bs 8 --kernels flashfusion --runtime triton --cuda 13.1 --arch sm92 --kv-prefetch on --warmup 20 --steps 200`
Sylvie: nice. what's the baseline (cuda12 sm89) numbers?
Maya: baseline (cuda12.3 sm89, native cuda kernels): throughput 115 tok/s, p99 latency 78ms. flashfusion triton on sm92 cuda13.1 => throughput 94 tok/s, p99 88ms. ~18% throughput drop, p99 +12ms.
Raj: ugh. any memory-growth logs? KV cache size oscillating?
Maya: yes — profiler shows repeated KV flushes every ~7 requests when `kv-prefetch on`. stack snippet from nvprof-ish tracing:
Maya: ```
KVCacheManager::evict_prefix() @ 0x7fdd
FlashFusionKernel::step() @ 0x5ab3
cudaMemcpyAsync H2D 12.3ms
``` 
Maya: looks like an alignment/stride issue causing extra memcpy on sm92/triton path.
Kevin: does the cuda-kernel build differ? triton uses segmented GEMM schedule that changed in 2.25. maybe that interacts with sm92 WARPs.
Sylvie: I ran a microbench: single-layer flashfusion reduce on sm92 cuda13.1 (cuda kernels) without triton runtime — no memcpy spikes, throughput ~112 tok/s. So triton path seems suspect.
Raj: could be a codegen divergence: triton rounding of shared memory tiling or dynamic shared size causing padding, which forces KV to be copied differently.
Maya: to reproduce locally: set `TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=info` and run with `--trace-kv` — you'll see repeated `kv_prefetch_miss` events in the trace.
bench-bot: test run 2378000000-01: 2048/bs8/flashfusion/triton/sm92/cuda13.1 -> FAIL: throughput drop observed. Artifact: s3://bench-artifacts/2378000000/trace.tar.gz
Kevin: thx — can we bisect triton versions? try triton 2.23 vs 2.25
Sylvie: I ran 2.23 quick: triton 2.23 on sm92 cuda13.1 improved throughput to 108 tok/s, p99 80ms. so regression introduced between 2.23->2.25.
Raj: interesting. any difference when switching `--kv-prefetch off`?
Maya: kv-prefetch off on triton 2.25 brings throughput ~110 tok/s (so similar to 2.23). suggests a prefetch codepath regression.
Kevin: OK hypothesis: triton codegen changed prefetch scheduling causing misaligned async memcpy on sm92 kernels. Next steps: 1) file a triton issue with minimal repro, 2) patch runtime to fallback to cuda kernels for prefetch on sm92, 3) add canary to rollout.
Maya: created minimal repro gist and attached to triton issue: https://gist.github.com/redwood/flashfusion-sm92-repro
Maya: opened internal ticket INF-4291 referencing this thread.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for runtime-config `prefetch_fallback: sm92->cuda_kernel` on cluster `dedicated-eu-1`.
Kevin: before we push fallback, can we add a quick heuristic: if memcpy_count_per_step > 3 then force cuda-kernel fallback. low-risk.
Sylvie: agree. added `--memcpy-threshold 3` flag in local branch, microbench shows no perf delta on sm89 and fixes sm92/triton case.
Raj: can you add unit test and a perf regression alert for p99 increase > 5% for attn route?
Maya: yep. adding test + alert. also dumping perf traces to s3 for postmortem.
Maya: summary: regression introduced in triton 2.25 + cuda13.1 on sm92 impacting FlashFusion prefetch; workaround is fallback to cuda kernels for prefetch or memcpy-threshold heuristic. next: triton PR and rollout of fallback.
Kevin: awesome, thanks. :thumbsup:
Sylvie: ping me when the canary finishes, I'll run Eval harness on production traces.
Maya: will do. tagging @Raj for postmortem once canary stable.
